correctness.rationale: For any symmetric supported stochastic P, cyclic averaging does not increase its operator-norm SLEM. A full Fourier diagonalization of the averaged kernel reduces the spectrum to even and odd endpoint frequency intervals. The three active constraints \(u=1-Ea\), \(v=1-Ua-2b\), \(w=-1+Va+2b\) combine with positive coefficients \(\alpha=(V-U)/E\), \(1\), \(1\) to certify \(\rho\ge(V-U)/(V+2E-U)\). The candidate \(a=2/D\), \(b=(E-U)/D\), \(h=(V+E-4)/D\) attains equality; h>0 and the omitted even-frequency lower constraint follows from \(F\le V+E-U\), checked algebraically for both parities. Positivity of all three multipliers ensures uniqueness within rotation-invariant kernels. Prism comparison is separately proved via analogous Fourier certificate; asymptotics follow Taylor expansions. verify_mobius.py ran successfully with 20439 assertions, not used as proof.

value.rationale: The Möbius ladder is a natural cubic circulant with ring and long-range matching edges. An explicit optimal stochastic walk with a small sharp dual certificate, a surprising parity rule under twisting (odd exact equality and swap of rung/holding masses, even strict gain by \(\pi^4/m^4\)), and an asymptotic fourfold gap improvement over the bare 2m-cycle with only \(O(m^{-2})\) rung probabilities are structurally motivated and enable direct optimal design. These claims are not merely existing prism formula substitutions, numerical tables, or arbitrary small finite changes.
